memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Sacrifice fellowship offerings there, eating them and rejoicing in the presence of the Lord your God. And you shall write very clearly all the words of this law on these stones you have set up." — Deut 27:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After the burnt offerings came the fellowship offerings — and with them, eating and rejoicing in the presence of the Lord. Worship was not meant to be grim or fearful. Once the sacrifice was made, the people sat down together and celebrated joyfully before their God. There was a feast, a shared meal, gladness in His presence.

This is a picture we should not miss. God is not a harsh master to be appeased and then avoided. He invites His people to rejoice in His presence, to enjoy Him. True worship, grounded in sacrifice, overflows into joy.

And notice the order. Joy came after the offering was made. The sacrifice secured the fellowship; then the feast could begin. This is the very heart of the gospel. Because Christ, our sacrifice, has been offered once for all (Heb 10:10), we are welcomed into God's presence not with dread but with joy. The feast is open to us.

Alongside the joy, God still wanted His words written "very clearly" — plainly enough for all to read. Joyful worship and clear truth belong together. We rejoice in God, and we hold fast to His Word. So don't reduce your faith to duty alone. Because of Christ's finished sacrifice, come and rejoice in the presence of your God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there joy in my relationship with God, or only duty?
2. How does Christ's sacrifice free me to rejoice in God's presence?
3. When did I last truly delight in worshipping the Lord?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that because of Christ's sacrifice I can rejoice in Your presence. Fill my worship with genuine joy, and help me hold Your Word clearly and dearly. Amen.
